source_text: Καὶ ἑκάστῳ γένει ἡ διαδοχὴ ἀπαράλλακτος καὶ ἀνεπίμικτος πρὸς ἑτέραν φύσιν. Οὐχ οἷαι τῶν ἡμιόνων ἐπὶ τῆς χέρσου, ἢ καί τινων ὀρνίθων ἐπιπλοκαὶ παραχαρασσόντων τὰ γένη. Οὐδὲν παρὰ τοῖς ἰχθύσιν ἐξ ἡμισείας ὥπλισται τοῖς ὀδοῦσιν, ὡς βοῦς παρ' ἡμῖν καὶ πρόβατον· οὐδὲ γὰρ μηρυκίζει τι παρ' αὐτοῖς, εἰ μὴ τὸν σκάρον μόνον ἱστοροῦσί τινες. Πάντα δὲ ὀξυτάταις ἀκμαῖς ὀδόντων καταπεπύκνωται, ἵνα μὴ τῇ χρονίᾳ μασήσει ἡ τροφὴ διαρρέῃ· ἔμελλε γὰρ, εἰ μὴ ὀξέως κατατεμνομένη τῇ γαστρὶ παρεπέμπετο, ἐν τῇ λεπτοποιήσει διαφορεῖσθαι παρὰ τοῦ ὕδατος. 7.3 Τροφὴ δὲ ἰχθύσιν ἄλλοις ἄλλη κατὰ γένος διωρισμένη. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἰλύϊ τρέφονται· οἱ δὲ τοῖς φυκίοις· ἄλλοι ταῖς βοτάναις ταῖς ἐντρεφομέναις τῷ ὕδατι ἀρκοῦνται. Ἀλληλοφάγοι δὲ τῶν ἰχθύων οἱ πλεῖστοι, καὶ ὁ μικρότερος παρ' ἐκείνοις βρῶμά ἐστι τοῦ μείζονος. Κἄν ποτε συμβῇ τὸν τοῦ ἐλάττονος κρατήσαντα ἑτέρου γενέσθαι θήραμα, ὑπὸ τὴν μίαν ἄγονται γαστέρα τοῦ τελευταίου. Τί οὖν ἡμεῖς οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἄλλο τι ποιοῦμεν ἐν τῇ καταδυναστείᾳ τῶν ὑποδεεσ τέρων; τί διαφέρει τοῦ τελευταίου ἰχθύος ὁ τῇ λαιμάργῳ φιλοπλουτίᾳ τοῖς ἀπληρώτοις τῆς πλεονεξίας αὐτοῦ κόλποις ἐναποκρύπτων τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς; Ἐκεῖνος εἶχε τὰ τοῦ πένη τος· σὺ τοῦτον λαβὼν μέρος ἐποιήσω τῆς περιουσίας σεαυτοῦ. Ἀδίκων ἀδικώτερος ἀνεφάνης, καὶ πλεονεκτικώτε ρος πλεονέκτου. Ὅρα μὴ τὸ αὐτό σε πέρας τῶν ἰχθύων ἐκδέξηται, ἄγκιστρόν που, ἢ κύρτος, ἢ δίκτυον. Πάντως γὰρ καὶ ἡμεῖς πολλὰ τῶν ἀδίκων διεξελθόντες, τὴν τελευταίαν τιμωρίαν οὐκ ἀποδρασόμεθα. Ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἐν ἀσθενεῖ ζῴῳ πολὺ τὸ πανοῦργον καὶ ἐπίβουλον καταμαθὼν, βούλομαί σε φυγεῖν τῶν κακούργων τὴν μίμησιν. Ὁ καρκῖνος τῆς σαρκὸς ἐπιθυμεῖ τοῦ ὀστρέου· ἀλλὰ δυσάλωτος ἡ ἄγρα αὐτῷ διὰ τὴν περιβολὴν τοῦ ὀστράκου γίνεται. Ἀρραγεῖ γὰρ ἑρκίῳ τὸ ἁπαλὸν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡ φύσις κατησφαλίσατο. Διὸ καὶ ὀστρακόδερμον προσηγόρευται. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ δύο κοιλότητες ἀκριβῶς ἀλλήλαις προσηρμοσμέναι τὸ ὄστρεον περιπτύσσονται, ἀναγκαίως ἄπρακτοί εἰσιν αἱ χηλαὶ τοῦ καρκίνου. Τί οὖν ποιεῖ; Ὅταν ἴδῃ ἐν ἀπηνέμοις χωρίοις μεθ' ἡδονῆς διαθαλπόμενον, καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἀκτῖνα τοῦ ἡλίου τὰς πτύχας ἑαυτοῦ διαπλώσαντα, τότε δὴ λάθρᾳ ψηφῖδα παρεμβαλὼν, διακωλύει τὴν σύμπτυξιν, καὶ εὑρίσκεται τὸ ἐλλεῖπον τῆς δυνάμεως διὰ τῆς ἐπινοίας περιεχόμενος. Αὕτη ἡ κακία τῶν μήτε λόγου μήτε φωνῆς μετεχόντων. Ἐγὼ δέ σε βούλομαι τὸ ποριστικὸν καὶ εὐμήχανον τῶν καρκίνων ζηλοῦντα, τῆς βλάβης τῶν πλησίον ἀπέχεσθαι. Τοιοῦτός ἐστιν ὁ πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν πορευόμενος δόλῳ, καὶ ταῖς τῶν πλησίον ἀκαιρίαις ἐπιτιθέμενος, καὶ ταῖς ἀλλοτρίαις συμφοραῖς ἐντρυφῶν. Φεῦγε τὰς μιμήσεις τῶν κατεγνωσμένων. Τοῖς οἰκείοις ἀρκοῦ. Πενία μετὰ αὐταρκείας ἀληθοῦς, πάσης ἀπολαύσεως τοῖς σωφρονοῦσι προτιμοτέρα. Οὐκ ἂν παρέλθοιμι τὸ τοῦ πολύποδος δολερὸν καὶ ἐπίκλοπον, ὃς ὁποίᾳ ποτ' ἂν ἑκάστοτε πέτρᾳ περιπλακῇ, τὴν ἐκείνης ὑπέρχεται χρόαν. Ὥστε τοὺς πολλοὺς τῶν ἰχθύων ἀπροόπτως νηχομένους τῷ πολύποδι περιπίπτειν, ὡς τῇ πέτρᾳ δῆθεν, καὶ ἕτοιμον γίνεσθαι θήραμα τῷ πανούργῳ. Τοιοῦτοί εἰσι τὸ ἦθος οἱ τὰς ἀεὶ κρατούσας δυναστείας ὑπερχόμενοι, καὶ πρὸς τὰς ἑκάστοτε χρείας μεθαρμοζόμενοι, μὴ ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς ἀεὶ προαιρέσεως βεβηκότες, ἀλλ' ἄλλοι καὶ ἄλλοι ῥᾳδίως γινόμενοι, σωφροσύνην τιμῶντες μετὰ σωφρόνων, ἀκόλαστοι δὲ ἐν ἀκολάστοις, πρὸς τὴν ἑκάστου ἀρέσκειαν τὰς γνώμας μετατιθέμενοι.
thought_title: Fish kinds, greed, and the crab's cunning
orientation: Basil continues his moral reading of sea creatures, contrasting the fixed kinds of fish with human greed and the craftiness of the crab and octopus.
pass_a_gloss: And for each kind the succession is unchangeable and unmixed toward another nature. Not such as the ones of the mules on the dry land, or also the couplings of certain birds that falsify the kinds. Nothing among the fish is armed halfway with teeth, as ox among us and sheep; for neither does anything chew the cud among them, except the scarus alone some report. But all are packed thick with sharpest points of teeth, so that the food may not flow away by the long chewing; for it was going to be, if not quickly cut up it was sent along to the stomach, in the fine dividing to be dispersed by the water. 7.3 And food for fish is different for different ones, divided according to kind. For some feed on mud; others on seaweed; others are content with the plants that grow in the water. But most of the fish are eaters of one another, and the smaller among them is food for the bigger. And if ever it happens that the one that overpowered the smaller becomes prey of another, they are brought under the one stomach of the last one. What then do we humans do anything different in the domination of the weaker? How does he differ from the last fish, the one who by gluttonous love of wealth hides away the weak in the insatiable folds of his greed? That one had the things of the poor man; you took this man and made him a part of your own surplus. You appeared more unjust than the unjust, and more greedy than the greedy. See that the same end of the fish does not await you, a hook somewhere, or a weel, or a net. For altogether we too, having gone through many of the unjust things, will not escape the final punishment. And already having learned in a weak animal the great cunning and treachery, I want you to flee the imitation of the wicked. The crab desires the flesh of the oyster; but the prey is hard to catch for it because of the covering of the shell. For with an unbreakable fence nature secured the softness of the flesh. Therefore it is called shell-skinned. And since two hollows fitted exactly to one another enfold the oyster, necessarily the claws of the crab are ineffective. What then does it do? When it sees it in windless places warming itself with pleasure, and having unfolded its folds toward the ray of the sun, then indeed secretly throwing in a pebble, it prevents the closing together, and the lack of strength is found to be overcome by the device. This is the wickedness of those that share neither reason nor voice. But I want you, emulating the resourcefulness and ingenuity of the crabs, to keep away from the harm of neighbors. Such is the one who goes to his brother with deceit, and attacks the inopportune moments of neighbors, and revels in the misfortunes of others. Flee the imitations of the condemned. Be content with your own things. Poverty with true self-sufficiency is more preferable to the self-controlled than every enjoyment. I would not pass over the deceitful and thievish thing of the octopus, which to whatever rock it ever clings, it takes on the color of that one. So that the many of the fish swimming without foresight fall upon the octopus, as upon the rock supposedly, and become ready prey for the cunning one. Such in character are those who take on the powers that always prevail, and adapt themselves to the needs of each occasion, not standing on the same choice always, but becoming different and different easily, honoring self-control with the self-controlled, but licentious among the licentious, changing their judgments toward the pleasing of each one.

choices.why: The source names a specific fish, σκάρος, which is the parrotfish or scarus; keeping the transliterated name preserves the specificity without importing a modern common name that might conflate species.
κύρτος is a basket-like fish trap; 'weel' is the traditional English term for this device, more precise than a generic 'trap'.
The compound means 'shell-skinned' literally, and Basil is explaining why the oyster is so named; the literal rendering preserves his etymological point.
ἀπήνεμος means 'sheltered from wind' or 'windless'; the literal rendering keeps the image of the oyster basking in calm, warm spots.
πτύξ means 'fold' or 'layer'; the oyster's shell halves are pictured as folds that open to the sun.
The phrase describes those who align themselves with whichever ruling power is currently dominant; the literal rendering keeps the temporal and political force.
rejected: the ruling powers of the moment

pass_b_english: For each kind the succession is unchangeable and unmixed with another nature. It is not like the mules on dry land, or the couplings of certain birds that falsify the kinds. Among fish nothing is armed with teeth only halfway, as the ox is among us and the sheep; for nothing among them chews the cud, except the scarus alone, as some report. All of them are packed thick with the sharpest points of teeth, so that their food may not slip away through prolonged chewing; for if it were not cut up quickly and sent on to the stomach, it would be dissolved in the fine dividing by the water.

The food of fish is different for different kinds, marked out according to kind. Some feed on mud; others on seaweed; others are satisfied with the plants that grow in the water. But most fish are eaters of one another, and among them the smaller is food for the larger. And if it ever happens that the one that overpowered the smaller becomes the prey of another, they are brought under the single stomach of the last one. What then do we human beings do differently in our domination of those who are weaker? How does the man differ from the last fish, who with gluttonous love of wealth hides the weak in the insatiable folds of his greed? That one had what belonged to the poor man; you took this and made it part of your own surplus. You have shown yourself more unjust than the unjust, and more greedy than the greedy. Beware lest the same end as the fish await you—some hook, or weel, or net. For certainly we too, after passing through many acts of injustice, will not escape the final punishment.

Now that I have observed in a weak animal the great cunning and treachery, I want you to flee the imitation of evildoers. The crab desires the flesh of the oyster; but the catch is hard for it to make because of the shell's covering. For nature has secured the soft flesh with an unbreakable fence. This is why it is called shell-skinned. And since two hollows fitted precisely to each other enfold the oyster, the claws of the crab are necessarily ineffective. What then does it do? When it sees the oyster in windless places warming itself with pleasure, and spreading out its folds toward the ray of the sun, then it secretly slips in a pebble and prevents the closing, and the deficiency of its power is found to be supplied by its cunning. This is the wickedness of creatures that share neither reason nor voice. But I want you, admiring the resourceful ingenuity of crabs, to refrain from harming your neighbors. Such is the one who proceeds against his brother with deceit, and attacks his neighbors in their moments of vulnerability, and revels in the misfortunes of others. Flee the imitations of those who stand condemned. Be content with what is your own. Poverty with true self-sufficiency is more precious to the wise than every enjoyment.

I would not pass over the deceit and trickery of the octopus, which takes on the color of whatever rock it clings to at any given time. So most fish, swimming without foresight, fall upon the octopus as if it were the rock, and become ready prey for the cunning creature. Such in character are those who go along with the powers that always prevail, and adapt themselves to each occasion's needs, never standing on the same fixed purpose, but easily becoming different people at different times—honoring self-control among the self-controlled, but licentious among the licentious, shifting their judgments to please each person.

problems.source_quote: ὑπὸ τὴν μίαν ἄγονται γαστέρα τοῦ τελευταίου
problems.why: English says 'both' but Greek says 'under the one stomach of the last one'—the smaller and its captor, not 'both' ambiguously
problems.fix: both are brought under the single stomach of the last one

problems.quote: That fish had the poor man's goods
problems.why: Ἐκεῖνος refers to the last fish (the predator), not 'that fish' as a generic; and 'the poor man's' not 'poor man's goods'—the Greek says 'the things of the poor man'
problems.fix: That one had what belonged to the poor man

problems.quote: you took him and made him a part of your own surplus
problems.source_quote: σὺ τοῦτον λαβὼν μέρος ἐποιήσω τῆς περιουσίας σεαυτοῦ
problems.why: τοῦτον refers to 'what belonged to the poor man,' not 'him' (the poor man); you took it and made it part of your surplus
problems.fix: you took this and made it part of your own surplus
problems.ruling: τοῦτον refers to the poor man's goods (τὰ τοῦ πένητος), not the poor man himself; 'him' misleads.

problems.fix: Beware lest the same end as the fish await you
problems.ruling: Ὅρα μὴ means 'beware lest'; 'See that...does not' inverts the warning's force.

The Greek 'Ἐκεῖνος εἶχε τὰ τοῦ πένητος' means 'That one had the things of the poor man,' referring to the last fish (the predator), not 'that fish had the poor man's goods.'
The Greek 'σὺ τοῦτον λαβὼν μέρος ἐποιήσω τῆς περιουσίας σεαυτοῦ' means 'you took this and made it part of your own surplus,' referring to the poor man's things, not 'you took him.'

last_rejected.why: κύρτος means 'basket-trap' or 'creel', not 'weel' (a fish-trap with specific Scottish associations).
last_rejected.ruling: κύρτος = basket-trap/creel; 'weel' is a valid English fish-trap term, within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: the insatiable folds of his greed
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῖς ἀπληρώτοις τῆς πλεονεξίας αὐτοῦ κόλποις
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'the insatiable folds of his greed' (κόλποις = folds/bosom), but 'his greed' is rendered as 'his greed'—wait, checking again: English has 'insatiable folds of his greed' which captures it. Rechecking: actually the English says 'insatiable folds of his greed'—this seems correct. Let me re-examine.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter retracted; English correctly renders τοῖς ἀπληρώτοις τῆς πλεονεξίας αὐτοῦ κόλποις.

last_rejected.why: δυναστείας here means 'ruling powers' or 'authorities' in the sense of those in power, but 'powers that always prevail' is awkward and slightly misleading—Basil means those who currently hold power, not abstract powers.
last_rejected.fix: the rulers who are in power at any time
last_rejected.ruling: τὰς ἀεὶ κρατούσας δυναστείας = 'powers that always prevail'; reasonable rendering of the Greek.

last_rejected.why: γνώμας means 'opinions' or 'minds'/'purposes', not 'judgments'. These are unprincipled people who change their whole stance, not just judicial decisions.
last_rejected.ruling: γνώμας = opinions/views/judgments; 'judgments' is within normal semantic range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: ὑπερχόμενοι means 'flattering' or 'courting favor with', not merely 'going along with'. The octopus changes color to deceive; these people flatter those in power.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπερχόμενοι = going under/submitting to; 'go along with' captures the sense adequately.
